I'll help you add a 👀 reaction to a message from someone in #mentorship-hub. Let me work through this step by step.

First, let me find the #mentorship-hub channel:

<action>
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&types=public_channel,private_channel&limit=100"
</action>

Now let me search for the mentorship-hub channel in the results and get its details, then I'll fetch its members:

<action>
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&types=public_channel,private_channel" | grep -i "mentorship-hub"
</action>

Let me get the channel info more directly:

<action>
curl -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&types=public_channel,private_channel&limit=200"
</action>

Let me check the full response and extract the channel ID properly:

<action>
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&types=public_channel,private_channel&limit=200" | python3 -m json.tool
</action>

Let me try a simpler approach - search for messages from the #mentorship-hub channel and add a reaction:

<action>
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/search.messages \
  -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&query=in%3Amentorship-hub&count=10"
</action>

Let me try getting conversations list and looking for mentorship-hub:

<action>
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&types=public_channel,private_channel" | jq '.channels[] | select(.name=="mentorship-hub") | .id'
</action>

Now let me get the members of that channel:

<action>
CHANNEL_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&types=public_channel,private_channel" | jq -r '.channels[] | select(.name=="mentorship-hub") | .id') && \
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.members \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&channel=$CHANNEL_ID" | jq '.members'
</action>

Now let me get the message history from that channel:

<action>
CHANNEL_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&types=public_channel,private_channel" | jq -r '.channels[] | select(.name=="mentorship-hub") | .id') && \
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.history \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&channel=$CHANNEL_ID&limit=10" | jq '.messages[0]'
</action>

Now let me add the 👀 reaction to the first message:

<action>
CHANNEL_ID=$(curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.list \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&types=public_channel,private_channel" | jq -r '.channels[] | select(.name=="mentorship-hub") | .id') && \
MESSAGE_TS=$(curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/conversations.history \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&channel=$CHANNEL_ID&limit=10" | jq -r '.messages[0].ts') && \
curl -s -X POST https://slack.com/api/reactions.add \
  -d "token=<TOKEN>&channel=$CHANNEL_ID&name=eyes&timestamp=$MESSAGE_TS"
</action>

<done>
I've added the 👀 (eyes emoji) reaction to a message from a member of the #mentorship-hub channel. The reaction was added to the most recent message in the channel.
</done>
